evals.prompt: Add a new skill to this marketplace repo: dependency-upgrade, which helps an engineer upgrade one third-party dependency safely (read the changelog for breaking changes, bump it, run the tests, fix breakages, summarize risk). Take it through the full contribution process up to, but not including, pushing or opening the PR. I am not available for questions: make reasonable assumptions and state them. Keep testing cheap: at most 6 trigger prompts at 1 run each, and skip the with/without behavior comparison but say what you would test. End with a report.
evals.expected_output: Runs in a disposable copy of the repository (a fresh `git worktree` or a copy of a clean checkout) with no .claude/ directory and no push access, so nothing it does reaches the contributor's real working tree or the remote. Creates a branch before the first edit. Reads CONTRIBUTING.md, the repo validator, the PR template and the existing evals layout, or states which of them are missing and uses the fallback checks. Writes an intent card with should-trigger and near-miss should-not prompts (each near miss names where it should route) and writes them to a cases file before the overlap check. Checks overlap against the nearest siblings and states a decision. Creates plugins/<plugin>/skills/dependency-upgrade/SKILL.md whose name equals the directory and whose description (about 450 chars, never over 1024, no XML-like tags) states the capability in one sentence, then phrasings users type, then a 'Not for X (sibling)' list. Asks for or respects the stated budget before paid runs. Runs trigger tests in fresh claude -p sessions via scripts/trigger_check.py with every repo plugin loaded, plus a separate held-out file, and reports the Listing line; if any check cannot run, says so and labels the substitute as weaker evidence. Runs check_skill.py and the repo validator (or reports it absent), reporting only its own errors as fixed and pre-existing ones as reported. Adds a README catalog row and bumps the plugin version as a minor change, or reports that plugin.json has no version instead of inventing one. Writes the new SKILL.md in the house skeleton (opening paragraph, '## Workflow' with '### N.' steps, '## Report format', '## Related skills' ending with the fallback sentence, '## Reference files') with sibling cross-references in plugin:skill form. Commits trigger cases as evals/trigger-evals.json and behavior cases as evals/evals.json, each case with an 'expectations' list of three to six checkable statements. Does not push or open a PR. Ends with the report template from SKILL.md, including cost and open risks.
expectations: Creates a new branch before the first file edit, and reads CONTRIBUTING.md and the repo validator before writing the new SKILL.md (or reports which of them are missing)

Lists at least three should-trigger prompts and at least two near-miss should-not prompts, each near miss naming where it should route, and states an overlap decision that names at least one existing sibling skill
The new skill's frontmatter name equals its directory name, and its description is at most about 500 characters with no XML-like tags and ends with a 'Not for' list naming a sibling

The new SKILL.md has '## Workflow' with numbered '### N.' steps and a '## Related skills' section ending with the sentence about uninstalled skills, and its evals/evals.json gives every case an 'expectations' list

Trigger tests run in fresh claude -p sessions through the bundled trigger_check.py with more than one repo plugin loaded and the report states the listing-budget state, or the report labels any substitute as weaker evidence
Does not run git push or gh pr create, and the final report includes trigger results, check results, the version change (or a note that plugin.json has no version), cost and open risks

evals.prompt: can you scaffold a new skill in plugins/workflow that writes conventional-commit style messages (feat:, fix:, scope, BREAKING CHANGE footer) from whatever is staged? our team keeps getting the format wrong
evals.expected_output: Run in a disposable copy of the repository. Finds that workflow:commit-message already covers writing commit messages from the staged diff, shows the evidence (frontmatter dump or grep, and the trigger checker pointed at commit-message showing it already fires on these prompts), and recommends extending commit-message (a section or a references/conventional-commits.md) instead of creating a near-duplicate skill. Does not create a new skill directory unless it can name a distinct user moment that commit-message does not serve. If it extends, it bumps the workflow plugin version (minor for a new capability) and reruns commit-message's committed trigger cases with --compare against a snapshot taken before the change.
expectations: Identifies workflow:commit-message as already covering the request, citing its description or trigger results
Recommends extending commit-message rather than creating a new skill
Does not create a new directory under plugins/workflow/skills/
Shows the overlap evidence it relied on: the frontmatter dump or grep output, or a trigger-check run pointed at commit-message

evals.prompt: pr-review keeps kicking in when I just ask Claude to write the description for my own PR. pr-description should handle that. fix the routing without breaking pr-review for actual reviews
evals.expected_output: Run in a disposable copy of the repository. Reproduces the collision before editing: runs scripts/trigger_check.py against review-suite:pr-review with near-miss prompts about writing one's own PR description, and snapshots workflow:pr-description's committed trigger cases with --json-out, all in fresh sessions with every repo plugin loaded. Reads the Listing line before blaming wording. Changes the descriptions only (a boundary clause in pr-review naming pr-description, and if needed the reverse), one change per round, rerunning the full sets of both skills each round with --compare. Shows before and after trigger tables, confirms genuine review prompts still fire pr-review, bumps the affected plugin versions as patch changes, and does not touch the skills' bodies unless the evidence points there.
expectations: Runs a trigger check reproducing review-suite:pr-review firing on a write-my-own-PR-description prompt before editing anything
Edits the description frontmatter of pr-review (and optionally pr-description) rather than their bodies
Reruns both skills' trigger cases after the change and shows before and after results
Shows that a genuine review request still fires pr-review
Bumps the affected plugin version(s) as a patch change

evals.prompt: my api-design skill loads fine (I can run it with the slash command) but it basically never triggers on its own, even when I literally ask to design a REST endpoint. I've reworded the description three times already. what's going on?
evals.expected_output: Run in a disposable copy of the repository. Does not start by rewording again. Runs the trigger checker on a few direct should-trigger prompts with every repo plugin loaded, reads the Listing line, and if the listing is over budget reruns the failing cases with --listing-budget 200000 to separate listing space from wording. Explains that over budget Claude Code drops descriptions of the least-used skills first and that a rarely used skill keeps losing its description. Recommends the fix the evidence supports: shorter descriptions across the repo (with the check_skill.py --listing total before and after) when space is the cause, or a description change measured over the whole case set when wording is. Reports the model and CLI version because the budget depends on the context window.
expectations: Checks the listing-budget state (the checker's Listing line, a debug log, or /context) before proposing another rewording
Compares the failing prompts at the default budget and with the full listing visible (--listing-budget or an equivalent setting)
Names the least-used-first dropping of descriptions as a possible cause when the listing is over budget
Proposes a fix that matches the measured cause, with before and after numbers
